title: Right of petition: how long do they have to respond?
excerpt: The law sets specific deadlines for entities to answer your petitions. Learn what they are and what to do if you do not get a response.
body:
The right of petition, recognized in article 23 of the Colombian Constitution, allows you to submit respectful requests to authorities and, in certain cases, to private parties, and to obtain a substantive response.

## Response deadlines

Law 1755 of 2015 sets the following deadlines, counted in business days from when the petition is received:

- **General rule:** 15 days.
- **Requests for documents and information:** 10 days.
- **Consultations:** 30 days.

If the entity cannot respond on time, it must say so before the deadline expires, explain why and set a new date, which cannot exceed twice the initial deadline.

## What if they do not respond?

Failing to respond violates a fundamental right. In that case you can file a **tutela action** so that a judge orders the entity to respond.

## Recommendations

- Keep the filing number or proof of submission.
- Be clear about what you are requesting.
- Attach the documents that support your petition.
